name: Frequency Studios and Instructors
note: Finds independent studios and the instructors who teach across them, and drafts one note each. Draft only. Ships off.

offer.pitch: A free page, class calendar and contact list for a studio or an instructor, in the town where they teach.
offer.call_to_action: Put your classes on the calendar

niches.label: Independent yoga, dance, fitness, martial arts and art studios

hunts.link_line: If you'd like a free page and class calendar on Frequency, start here:

playbook.seek: Who to find: independent studios in the region and the instructors who teach in them: yoga, pilates, dance, martial arts, movement, climbing, pottery, art and music studios with a public class schedule, and instructors whose own page lists classes at two or more places. Use niche "studio" for a studio and "instructor" for a person.
playbook.signals: Strong signs, best first: a public weekly schedule with several teachers on it; an intro offer or a first-class-free line; workshops or series beyond the regular schedule; a teachers page with names; an instructor's own site listing where they teach this week. Weak signs: a schedule that has not changed in months, or a studio that is one location of a chain.
playbook.where: Where to look: studio websites and their schedule, workshops and teachers pages, instructors' own websites, city recreation listings, and class pages on Eventbrite and Meetup.
playbook.queries: Searches that work: "<town> yoga studio schedule", "<town> dance studio adult classes", "<town> pilates studio", "<town> martial arts adult classes", "<town> pottery studio classes", "<town> yoga teacher classes", "<studio name> teachers". Use each area's own town names.
playbook.skip: Skip national chains and franchises, big-box gyms, kids-only programs, online-only studios and teacher trainings.
playbook.rank: Order leads.json best first, because only the first few are kept: an independent studio with several teachers on a live schedule and a listed email comes first, then an instructor who teaches at two or more places and lists a contact, then the rest. One lead per studio or instructor, addressed to the person who runs it when the page names them.
playbook.record: In leads.json the event is their class offering: event.title is the studio's name or the kind of class, event.url is the public schedule or classes page, and starts_at may be empty. The organizer is the studio owner or the instructor.
playbook.note: Write a warm, human invite in four short paragraphs. 1: "Hi <first name>, your <studio or the kind of class they teach, named loosely> caught my eye, and I love what you are up to." You may add one short, true line about it and one emoji that fits them; never give a date, time, price or address, and never comment on how full a class is. 2: "I'm Daniel, a local community builder and the founder of Frequency!" 3: "Frequency is a free way for neighbors to find or start local, in-person Circles and events around what they love. Right now I'm focused on the studios and teachers who bring people together in person, and on making it easy for places like yours to be found by the people who live nearby." 4: one easy question that fits them, such as "Would you be interested in sharing your classes with neighbors nearby who would love them?", then "We're beta launching here in North County SD, and I would love for you to come check it out." Keep the quoted sentences as written. Use no exclamation mark besides the one in paragraph 2, and in a DM leave out the "Right now" sentence.

hunts.name: Studios and instructors
hunts.looking_for: Independent studios in North County San Diego with a public class schedule, and instructors who teach at two or more local places
